summary: Cummings-Coleman is absent from Thursday’s report, while Amachree, Willis and Thurman are listed out. At Utah, follow the available backfield workload and make sure Parker stays accounted for when he releases into a route.

items.headline: Cummings-Coleman is off Thursday’s report; three Kansas backs are out
items.tldr: The Big 12 report lists Amachree, Willis and Thurman out, with Moses doubtful. Cummings-Coleman’s absence from the report leaves his workload to be observed, rather than assumed.

items.headline: Edwards delivered 137 rushing yards and three touchdowns
items.tldr: The Middle Tennessee game showed he could carry a larger workload. Watch whether the blocking gives him a useful first cut against Utah.

items.headline: Kansas needs cleaner kickoff coverage after two long returns
items.tldr: Middle Tennessee returned consecutive kicks for 38 and 52 yards up the right sideline. Watch the kick placement and lane assignments against Utah.

items.headline: Utah’s Parker has scored as both runner and receiver
items.tldr: Utah’s preview lists touchdowns in both roles. Account for him after the snap, especially when a short throw can replace a running play.

items.headline: Kansas–Kansas State is set for 11 a.m. CT on October 17
items.tldr: FS1 will carry the game in Manhattan. First comes the late trip to Utah; plan for the quick change in viewing time the following week.

lead.headline: Make the backfield assignments work.
lead.body: Watch who carries, who protects and who provides a short receiving option. On defense, keep a defender attached when Utah’s back leaves the backfield.

matchup.thesis: Track the back on both sides
matchup.question: What should Kansas emphasize at Utah?
matchup.answer: Follow the active Kansas backs through carries and pass protection. On defense, account for Parker after the snap and finish the tackle before a short throw becomes a long gain.
